video.title: Forget AI. Make $10K+ With These Offline Side Hustles

summary: Chris Koerner and Brandon Doyle walk through five offline side hustles framed around making $10K in a year, month, week or day: temporary construction fence rental, portable mini-mini-golf (and cornhole golf) rentals/installs, inflatable outdoor movie rentals, buying local original art abroad to resell, and flipping a pallet of auction rugs. The fullest case is Brandon's teenage son, who bought 115 auction rugs for about $1,500 and sold about 80 for over $3,000 to fund a first car. The fence story is second-hand and the others are mostly observed or hypothetical. The takeaway is that low-tech, rent-or-resell businesses have cheap entry and fast payback, but almost all need physical work.

speakers.description: Host of The Koerner Office; runs business-idea content and sells business plans/membership.

ideas.name: Temporary construction fence rental
ideas.one_liner: Rent temporary fencing panels to new construction sites, charged per linear foot per month.
ideas.business_model: Rental of owned panels, priced per linear foot per month with discounts for longer terms; deposits upfront.
ideas.customer: Construction site managers and general contractors on new builds without fencing.
ideas.problem: Sites legally or for liability reasons need perimeter fencing, and builders do not want to buy it.
ideas.offer: Delivery, set-up and removal of temporary fence panels at a low rental rate.

pricing.model: Per linear foot per month, tapering with duration

price_points.unit: per linear foot (per month, as assumed)
price_points.label: starting rate

pricing.notes: Hosts assumed the rates are monthly; contract total may be paid in instalments or 50-75% upfront.

acquisition_channels.details: Friend drove around, found new construction sites without fencing, went to the site trailer and pitched the person in charge. Hosts also suggest calling the number on the contractor's banner.

quote.text: he would just go to construction sites that are new that didn't have any temporary fencing up yet and he would just say, "Do you want a temporary fence? I'll rent you mine."
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

acquisition_channels.details: Call the number on the construction banner; also idea of using public building permits to get ahead of site start.

ideas.delivery: Owner and crew set up fence in about a day and remove it months later; no maintenance or cleaning in between.
unit_economics_claims: Sold the company for $600K after 18 months
Several hundred thousand made before sale
ideas.startup_cost: Cost of buying panels; idea is to sell the first job and then buy fencing, so possibly near zero upfront.
ideas.time_to_first_revenue: Quick: sell first job, then buy panels and install within a day

acquisition.how: Site visits are in person; permit-data lead lists and calling businesses could be partly automated, but the friend's route is physical.

onboarding.how: Quotes and contracts can be templated and e-signed, with a human confirming site details.

delivery.how: Trucks, crews and physical panel installation and removal.

billing.how: Invoicing and instalment billing is easily automated.

support.how: Occasional site issues need a person on site.

uk_applicability.notes: Hoarding and Heras-style fence hire already exists in the UK; local planning rules and the incumbent hire companies differ but the model carries over.

risks: Payment is spread over months, so cash flow is slower than headline job value

quotes.text: He made several hundred grand while doing it and then sold the company for 600 grand 18 months later, which he said he now regrets
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

quotes.text: for max two days at the very start and two days at the very end, you're working. Yeah. And for the rest, you're just collecting a check.
quotes.speaker: Brandon Doyle

ideas.name: Portable mini-mini-golf hole rentals and sales
ideas.one_liner: Build small portable mini golf holes and rent them to events or sell them.
ideas.business_model: Per-hole daily rental to events, plus direct sale of units.
ideas.customer: Weddings, parties and events; individuals buying a course.
ideas.problem: Events want unique entertainment without hiring a large venue.
ideas.offer: Portable holes of 2x4 frame, astroturf and obstacles on plywood.

pricing.model: Per hole per day rental; sale price per unit

price_points.label: sale price, up to close to $1,000

pricing.notes: Sale price described as hundreds up to about $1,000.

acquisition_channels.details: Listed for free on Facebook Marketplace.

quote.text: His customer acquisition channel is free because it costs nothing to post them and it's paid for and anything after that is just gravy.
quote.speaker: Brandon Doyle

ideas.delivery: Build the holes from lumber, turf and plywood; deliver and collect them for each event.
unit_economics_claims: $300 per hole per day rental is more than material cost
Rent 35 holes a month to reach $10K
Materials repaid in about three months
ideas.startup_cost: Materials per hole, less than $300 per hole claimed

acquisition.how: Marketplace listings and replies can be agent-managed.

onboarding.how: Booking forms and deposits can be automated.

delivery.how: Building, transporting and setting up physical holes.

support.how: Chatbot handles most; damage or event-day issues need a person.

uk_applicability.notes: Facebook Marketplace and event hire exist in the UK; check public liability insurance.

risks: Transport and storage of bulky items

quotes.text: renting them out to weddings, events, parties, etc. for $300 per hole per day, which is less than the cost of the materials, right?
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.name: Cornhole mini golf install for RV parks
ideas.one_liner: Design and install themed cornhole-hole courses at RV parks and sell/rent boards.
ideas.business_model: One-off install fee per hole plus optional small monthly maintenance fee; alternatively sell or rent boards.
ideas.customer: RV parks and similar amenity venues.
ideas.problem: Venue owners want amenities but not the headache of designing obstacles.
ideas.offer: Turnkey cornhole course with obstacles on any walkable ground.

pricing.model: Per hole install fee plus optional monthly maintenance

acquisition_channels.details: Show RV park owners their own website with a pitch; also Facebook Marketplace route for sales/rental.

ideas.delivery: Build and install boards and obstacles on site; periodic check-ups.

acquisition.how: Cold email to limited companies is permitted; RV parks may be sole traders, so check.

onboarding.how: Site design and agreement need human input.

uk_applicability.notes: Cornhole is less known in the UK, and campsite/caravan parks differ; demand untested.

risks: Untested concept: seen once at one RV park

quotes.text: I do this for you. I charge $700 per hole and it's yours forever.
quotes.speaker: Brandon Doyle

ideas.name: Inflatable outdoor movie rentals
ideas.one_liner: Rent inflatable screen, projector and speakers for backyard and HOA movie nights.
ideas.customer: Backyard parties, birthday parties, HOAs, neighbourhood events.
ideas.problem: Families want an easy outdoor movie experience at events.
ideas.offer: Delivered or set-up inflatable screen with projector and Bluetooth speakers.

acquisition_channels.details: Facebook Marketplace implied by the theme.

ideas.delivery: Transport and set up screen, projector, speakers at the event.
unit_economics_claims: Southern Outdoor Cinema does $3-4M a year after 17 years

acquisition.how: SEO, local listings and marketplaces suit inbound.

support.how: Mostly chat; on-the-day issues need a person.

uk_applicability.notes: UK has outdoor cinema hire; weather is less reliable and HOAs are less common.

quotes.text: you can buy all of this equipment for 500 to 3,000 bucks.
quotes.speaker: Brandon Doyle

quotes.text: you pay off all your equipment in like one to six rentals.
quotes.speaker: Brandon Doyle

ideas.name: Bounce house rentals
ideas.one_liner: Inflatable bounce house hire, with the angle of cleaning every rental.
ideas.problem: Existing operators are poorly run and their equipment is not cleaned.
ideas.offer: Bounce houses that are cleaned between each rental.
ideas.delivery: Deliver, set up and clean inflatables.
unit_economics_claims: Operators are raking in cash every weekend

uk_applicability.notes: Bouncy castle hire is established in the UK, and safety inspection (e.g. PIPA) is required.

quotes.text: if you just clean your bounce houseses between every rental, you will be in the top 10%.
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.name: Overseas local-art arbitrage
ideas.one_liner: Buy original local art abroad cheaply, by travelling or remote, and resell at home at several times the price.
ideas.business_model: Buy low abroad, resell at a markup via Instagram and Facebook Marketplace.
ideas.customer: Home-country buyers wanting unique original art.
ideas.problem: Unique originals are not available locally or online.
ideas.offer: Curated original art from local shops abroad.

pricing.notes: Purchase cost is a guess by the host.

acquisition_channels.details: Dedicated Instagram account promoted from a personal account, selling in waves.
Facebook Marketplace listings, possibly with preorders and deposits.

ideas.delivery: Phone or FaceTime shops, buy and ship rolled art, then ship or hand over to buyers.

acquisition.how: Content and listings can be agent-run.

uk_applicability.notes: Works in reverse for a UK person importing from abroad; consider import VAT and customs duty.

risks: Selling unlisted stock that is then sold elsewhere

quotes.text: even if she bought it for 50 and is selling for 400
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.name: Vintage watch and local goods arbitrage from abroad
ideas.one_liner: Same remote-sourcing model applied to vintage watches, apparel or regional foods from places like Japan.
ideas.business_model: Buy abroad via video calls or photos, list locally on Marketplace at a markup.
ideas.customer: Collectors and buyers of unique items.
ideas.problem: Hard to access unique foreign items.

acquisition_channels.details: Facebook Marketplace plus social content so algorithms find buyers.

ideas.delivery: Buy from foreign shop and ship to buyer.

uk_applicability.notes: Import VAT and duty apply; Vinted, eBay and Marketplace are alternatives.

quotes.text: If you can find a watch in Japan for 40 bucks, send you a picture of it, and then find me on Facebook Marketplace, and I'd be willing to pay 80
quotes.speaker: Chris Koerner

ideas.name: Auction rug flipping
ideas.one_liner: Buy bulk rug lots at online auction and resell individually via Facebook Marketplace and a garage sale.
ideas.business_model: Buy wholesale lots, resell individually at a markup.
ideas.customer: Local buyers looking for rugs on Facebook Marketplace and at a garage sale.
ideas.problem: People need rugs and want them cheaper than retail.

acquisition_channels.details: Sold through the father's Facebook Marketplace account, with a note that the seller is his son.
One garage sale advertised as a massive rug sale with signs around town sold roughly 40 rugs.

ideas.delivery: Buyers pick up in person from the barn; seller photographs rugs, lists and negotiates.

acquisition.how: Listings can be agent-assisted but photography is physical.

onboarding.how: Buyer messaging is automatable but pickup is arranged by a person.

delivery.how: Heavy goods handled and handed over in person.

uk_applicability.notes: Liquidation and returns pallets are available in the UK (eBay, auction sites); storage space needed.

risks: Storage and handling of heavy goods

tactics.name: Sell the job before buying inventory
steps: Pitch and close the first construction site job
Take a deposit upfront (possibly 50-75%)
Use the deposit to buy the fence panels
Install in about a day

quote.text: don't go buy your fencing first. Sell your first job. Yeah. Then go buy your fencing.
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

tactics.name: Find fence leads from signage and permits
steps: Notice sites about to start while driving
Call the number on the contractor's banner
Mention you have the best rates in the city and ask who to talk to
Optionally monitor public building permits to reach sites weeks ahead

tactics.name: Duration-tiered pricing
steps: Charge about $4 per linear foot
Reduce towards $2 per foot for longer rentals
Expect jobs to overrun to your advantage

tactics.name: Remote art sourcing via photos and preorders
steps: Find local shops on Google
Call and ask for close-up photos by WhatsApp
List on Facebook Marketplace at a markup
Collect deposits and warn of 2-4 week delivery
Then pay the shop and ship rolled in a tube

tactics.name: Clearance-lot flipping with a worst-case floor
steps: Check local Marketplace prices first
Buy only if worst-case average resale beats cost
Sell via Marketplace plus a themed garage sale with road signs
Upsell low-value items such as doormats at the sale

tactics.name: Photograph inventory well
steps: Roll the item out on a clean indoor background
Use one rug turned upside down as a backdrop for others
Avoid grass or dirt backgrounds

warnings.warning: Rug buyer did no demand research before buying and had to hold heavy stock in storage; winter is the worst selling season.

warnings.warning: Pre-selling art remotely risks selling something that is then sold elsewhere, requiring refunds.

quote.text: the only downside to that is you could sell something that was then bought
quote.speaker: Chris Koerner

warnings.warning: Passive rental businesses can become boring to run, leading to early sale of the company.

lessons.lesson: Teach young people via small asset-light flips with a capped downside; set the worst-case resale price above cost before buying.

quote.text: if we can get these for like 12 to 13 bucks worst case scenario we sell them for an average of 20 bucks.
quote.speaker: Brandon Doyle

lessons.lesson: Rental assets with cheap equipment pay back in a few rentals, then become mostly profit.

quote.text: you pay off all your equipment in like one to six rentals.
quote.speaker: Brandon Doyle

lessons.lesson: Selling before buying inventory removes capital risk.
Free marketplaces can be the entire acquisition channel for local rental or resale.
Competing on a simple trust promise (clean every time) can differentiate in sloppy industries.
Cross-border arbitrage has endless combinations of countries and product types because markets are never fully efficient.
In-person sales help conversion and upsells, as seen at the garage sale.
Hands-on selling teaches photography, negotiation, pricing and upselling skills.
Content that reaches an algorithm-matched audience can work even with few views.

evidence_quality.rationale: Mostly second-hand stories (friend's fence company, sister-in-law's art) and hypothetical math. The rug flip is first-hand with specific numbers but is a small, one-off, unverifiable family anecdote. Fence income appears to be monthly versus job totals, and the hosts themselves note ambiguity.
evidence_quality.promotional_conflict: Chris Koerner sells $19 business plans and a $5/month membership; Beehive sponsor read in the middle.
